title: midshift-latency-retrospective-and-followups-2026-07-12
content:
Shift window: 03:00-11:00 UTC, 2026-07-12. Owner: Priya Rao (oncall). Purpose: concise handoff + retrospective for a midshift latency incident that degraded p95/p99 for a subset of hosted inference traffic (models: gpt-mid-7b-q4, gpt-embed-2). This doc is intentionally informal — notes to next shift and action items.

Summary (tl;dr):
- 03:45 UTC: Alerts triggered (p95 HTTP latency > 450ms, p99 > 1.2s) for hosted-api route /v1/generate serving gpt-mid-7b-q4.
- 03:45-04:15: Oncall triage (me + Diego). Initial mitigation: disabled autoscale burst policy for the affected Dedicated pool and forced a gradual scale-up from 12 -> 40 GPUs.
- 04:10: Applied temporary routing fallback to gpt-mid-7b-q4-quantized variant for new sessions to reduce per-token CPU+GPU overhead.
- 05:30: Kernel-level scheduling patch rolled forward (runtime PR #891) to fix an inefficient batching edge-case; patch reverted a pathological batching stall that appeared only under mixed short/long request workloads.
- 06:00: Traffic and latency stabilized back within SLOs.

Timeline & key observations:
- 03:40 UTC: First alert chain from observability: p95 increased from baseline ~120ms -> 480ms. Error rate unchanged (4xx/5xx stable) which suggested not an application crash but a latency/backpressure issue.
- 03:42 UTC: Checked autoscaler signals: rapid up/down activity on serve-pool-prod-12 (spike of requests then cooldowns) — autoscaler entered burst window and spawned ephemeral pods with low warm cache.
- 03:47 UTC: Router traces indicated repeated queueing inside the runtime batching layer; KV-cache hit-rate for long-lived sessions dropped to 38% vs baseline ~85%.
- 03:55 UTC: Attempted config tweak to increase batching timeout from 10ms -> 20ms (to allow larger batches). This reduced p95 marginally but caused higher p50 for short requests. Rolled back at 04:05.
- 04:10 UTC: Disabled autoscale burst (temporary mitigation) and invoked scale-up to warm GPUs; this restored KV cache warmup and reduced queueing.
- 04:30 UTC: Deployed runtime PR #891 which includes a scheduler guard to avoid forming pathological micro-batches when short and long requests interleave.

Root-cause hypothesis (current):
- Primary: Autoscale burst policy spawned cold workers that never warmed KV cache; mixed workload (many short prompt completions alongside a few long context generations) caused the scheduler to create many small batches that incurred disproportionate overhead. The runtime scheduler had a corner-case where certain sequence-length distributions created repeated micro-batch churn (seen in traces).
- Secondary contributing: Alert thresholds for queueing/backpressure were tuned too lax, so early warning was delayed until client-facing latency hit p95 SLO.

What we tried (and why):
- Increase batching timeout (temporary): Tried to favor throughput over latency to build larger batches. Negative regression for short-tail requests -> rolled back.
- Disable autoscale burst and forcibly scale (temporary): Warming GPUs fixed KV cache coldness and reduced batch churn.
- Runtime scheduling patch PR #891: Fixes the micro-batching edge-case; small, targeted change that added a guard to prefer small fixed-size batches for known short requests and to preemptively chunk long requests.

What worked:
- Forced warm-up (scale-up) + fallback to quantized variant gave fastest recovery path.
- Runtime scheduler patch reduced recurring micro-batch formation in our test traffic and in production after rollout.

Open/Ongoing issues:
- Some customer sessions routed during 03:45-04:20 experienced higher-than-normal latency; incident window for affected sessions: ~03:40-05:10. Need to surface to CS for customer outreach (see action items).
- Autoscale policy still needs a small redesign: the burst mode is useful but should be gated with warm-cache heuristics.

Immediate action items (owners + suggested due dates):
- SRE: Tune queueing/backpressure alert thresholds to trigger at earlier signal (add a composite alert: KV cache hit-rate < 60% AND batch queue length > 8). Owner: Priya Rao. Due: 2026-07-14. Linked ticket: JIRA-SRE-4532.
- Runtime: Merge follow-up validation from PR #891 into canary and run 48h mixed-workload soak test. Owner: Diego Marquez. Due: 2026-07-16. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/891.
- Infra: Rework autoscale burst gating to require warm-cache estimate or minimum warm worker count before allowing burst. Owner: Marcus Li. Due: 2026-07-23. Linked artifact: infra-issue-2026-88.
- Observability: Add a dashboard tile for per-model kv-cache hit-rate and synthetic short/long workload latency breakdown. Owner: Hannah Kim. Due: 2026-07-15.
- CS/Support: Identify customers with requests routed during incident window for proactive outreach. Owner: Lena Novikova. Due: 2026-07-13.

Runbook notes & required updates: (quick stubs for next pass)
- Add a new play: \"Autoscale-burst warmup\" describing steps to check KV cache hit-rate, how to force warm GPUs, and when to toggle burst back on. (Section: Serving runtime -> autoscaler).
- Clarify escalation: If p95 > 400ms for > 10min AND kv-cache < 50%, escalate to runtime lead (Diego) instead of SRE manager. Current runbook mentions only oncall manager.
- Include a safe rollback checklist for runtime scheduler patches: canary steps, traffic percentage thresholds, and rollback commands.

Communication & escalation log (short):
- 03:46 UTC: Pager->oncall Priya (me). Slack thread #sre-ops: started.
- 03:50 UTC: Paged runtime oncall Diego (pinged pager).
- 04:05 UTC: Pinged infra (Marcus) to prepare capacity for forced scale.
- 04:12 UTC: Deployed quantized fallback routing for new sessions. Notified Product and CS channels.
- 05:35 UTC: Confirmed stability; posted summary in #sre-ops and #hosting-status.

Follow-ups for next shift (what I want you to check early):
- Monitor kv-cache hit-rate for gpt-mid-7b-q4: ensure sustained > 75% after autoscale policy re-enabled.
- Watch for any reappearance of micro-batch patterns in traces (look for repeated small batch ids in runtime logs).
- Verify canary of PR #891 remains stable for 24h (observability will create canary alert).
- Confirm CS outreach status and whether any customers opened support tickets related to this window.

Notes to self / informal pointers:
- The quantized fallback really helped reduce CPU jitter for short jobs; consider formalizing a \"fallback-first\" route for specific SLAs.
- We should add a synthetic probe that alternates short/long requests to exercise scheduler mixing; run nightly for 7 days after patch merge.

Attachments & references:
- Runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/891
- Jira: JIRA-SRE-4532 (alert tuning + post-incident tasks)
- Confluence playbook page (draft): confluence://pages/LATENCY-PLAYBOOK
- Slack thread: slack://archives/C01234567/s1678654321000 (see messages 4-12)

If anything regresses during your shift, ping Diego directly (pager) and escalate to Marcus for infra capacity. I'll be reachable until 12:30 UTC today if you need context.

End of handoff.

-- Priya
